demand.reason: Global palladium mine production was about 190 metric tons in 2025, placing it within the negligible-demand band of ≤500 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is projected to stagnate and flatline. Its primary autocatalyst application is eroding under internal price substitutions towards platinum and structural industry transitions towards zero-catalyst battery electric vehicles.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Primary extraction is split between Russia (84 of 190 tons in 2025, 44%) and South Africa (37%). Because Russia is the largest single producer, mining diversity aligns with the 30–50% band (Score 2).


Refining: Downstream refinement mirrors primary extraction, with Russia retaining domestic processing of its output. The largest processor paces strictly within the 30–50% band (Score 2).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Global PGM resources represent centuries of supply. Against current extraction volumes, the embedded palladium fraction is effectively limitless (>100 years).


Diversification: Total global reserves yield a calculated HHI of about 0.70, with South Africa holding about 83% of the PGM reserve base (63,000 of >76,000 tons). The geographic endowment matches the highly concentrated maximum score.

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): utilized widely in military electronics, precision sensors, and hydrogen storage systems. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): serves as the primary catalytic agent across the global gasoline vehicle fleet. Advanced Semiconductors & Computing (+1.0): forms the basis of multilayer ceramic capacitors and hard-disk platings. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): incorporated pervasively into dental alloys and brachytherapy seeds. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): acts as a bulk chemical synthesis catalyst for petroleum refining.


Sector presence scores total 5.0 across 5 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +2.0, yielding an objective composite score of 7.0.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Platinum acts as a widespread, commercially deployed substitute within catalytic converters, matching criteria for commercial deployment with manageable performance or cost trade-offs (Score 2).


Recyclability: Global secondary production from spent autocatalysts is highly mature and economically efficient, supplying nearly a third of total consumption and tracking in the >40% high recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Palladium extraction demands identical processes to platinum: deep, hazardous shaft mining followed by smelting and highly complex, multi-stage solvent extraction separations, classifying it as a specialized chemical barrier.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate but sluggish due to poor base pricing. Incremental outputs tied to secondary South African and Zimbabwean asset expansions are capable of adding 10–20% to supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India possesses zero commercial domestic extraction of palladium, leaving its vast catalytic and electronics sectors 100% import-dependent (Score 5).


Strategic Posture: Palladium is formally tracked on India's critical minerals list and is recovered from spent catalysts by Indian refiners such as Hindustan Platinum; the ₹1,500 crore recycling scheme (2025) covers catalytic converters. Lacking KABIL mandates or binding foreign equity agreements, India's posture aligns with early-stage declared strategic intent (Score 3).

price_volatility.reason: Palladium prices experienced highly volatile structural swings, dropping over 60% from a peak of $2,419/oz to $980/oz across a short timeline. Multi-year movements consistently exceed the >100% variance threshold, proving procurement instability.

capability.name: Palladium
capability.next_move: Grow recycling: secure spent catalysts and scrapped converters for Indian refiners, and assess the Boula-Nuasahi deposit.
capability.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: Russia 84 of 190 t (2025); South Africa 70 t; Canada 16 t; Zimbabwe 15 t.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.
Johnson Matthey (Manesar, 25 million autocatalysts made by 2014) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts with imported metal.
Primary metal is entirely imported (IBM); vehicle catalysts and electronics.

strategyList.name: Recycling (batteries, magnets, catalysts, PV)
strategyList.what: Shredding and hydrometallurgy of black mass; magnet recovery; spent-catalyst leaching; PV-panel recovery.
strategyList.outside_china: Battery recycling: China has over three-quarters of pre-treatment and 90% of material-recovery capacity; Europe, Japan, Korea and the US smaller.
strategyList.cost: India's scheme expects ~Rs 8,000 crore for 270+ kt/yr of capacity (~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr), yielding ~40 kt/yr of critical minerals.
strategyList.india_base: Lohum, Rubamin, the Bhopal magnet facility, CSIR-NML; Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme (2025).

chemistryList.name: Catalysts and spent-catalyst recovery
chemistryList.who: Rubamin (Mo, Co, Ni from spent catalyst); Hindustan Platinum (PGM refining).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Molybdenum and cobalt recovery; catalyst-grade chemicals.
chemistryList.summary: Spent catalysts are concentrated secondary sources of useful metals. India already has industrial experience recovering molybdenum and other metals, alongside precious-metal refining. The opportunity is to connect traceable waste collection, selective recovery and customer-approved products, while distinguishing regeneration from destruction and metal recovery.

links.how: Hindustan Platinum makes precious-metal catalysts and recovers platinum-group metals from used ones; it names platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium among the metals it refines.
